units.zh: 樂誌上
units.en: Treatise on Music, Part One
units.literal: Treatise on Music, Part One

units.zh: 古之王者，理定制禮，功成作樂，所以昭事天地，統和人神，歷代已來，舊章斯在。
units.en: The kings of old established ritual once order was settled and composed music once their achievements were complete, thereby making clear their service to Heaven and Earth and harmonizing the realms of human and spirit. From age to age, those ancient regulations have endured.
units.literal: The ancient kings, when order was settled established ritual, when achievements were complete made music, thereby to manifest service to Heaven and Earth and harmonize human and divine beings; from successive ages onward, the old regulations have remained in place.

units.zh: 洎唐季之亂，鹹、鎬為墟；
units.en: When the late Tang fell into chaos, the ritual centers at Xian and Hao were reduced to ruins;
units.literal: When the disorder of the late Tang came, Xian and Hao became ruins;

units.zh: 梁運雖興，《英》、《莖》掃地。
units.en: and though the Liang dynasty rose in their place, the ancient pieces Ying and Jing vanished entirely.
units.literal: though the fortune of Liang arose, the Ying and Jing pieces were swept clean from the earth.

units.zh: 莊宗起於朔野，經始霸圖，其所存者，不過邊部鄭聲而已，先王雅樂，殆將泯絕。
units.en: Zhuangzong rose from the northern marches and set about his bid for dominion, yet all that survived in his court was the vulgar Zheng music of the frontier; the elegant music of former kings was all but lost.
units.literal: Zhuangzong rose from the northern frontier and began his hegemonic design; what he preserved was nothing but the Zheng music of the borderlands, while the elegant music of the former kings was nearly extinguished.

units.zh: 當同光、天成之際，或有事清廟，或祈祀泰壇，雖簨虡猶施，而宮商孰辨？
units.en: During the Tongguang and Tiancheng reigns, rites were still held at the imperial temple or prayers offered at the great altar, but though ritual frames and plumes were set in place, who could tell one pitch from another?
units.literal: In the Tongguang and Tiancheng eras, sometimes there were rites at the Clear Temple or prayers at the great altar; though feathered frames were still set up, who could distinguish gong from shang?

units.zh: 遂使磬襄、鼗武，入河、漢而不歸；
units.en: Thus masters such as Qixiang and Taowu went off to the Yellow and Han and never came back;
units.literal: Thus masters like Qixiang and Taowu entered the Yellow and Han rivers and did not return;

units.zh: 湯、舜韶，混陵谷而俱失。
units.en: and the Shao music of Tang of Shang and Shun of Yu was swallowed up with the hills and valleys, lost without trace.
units.literal: the Shao music of Tang and Shun was mingled with hills and valleys and lost together.

units.zh: 洎晉高祖奄登大寶，思迪前規，爰詔有司，重興二舞。
units.en: When Jin Gaozu at last took the throne, he sought to follow the precedents of old and ordered the responsible offices to revive the two ritual dances.
units.literal: When Jin Gaozu suddenly ascended the great throne, he thought to follow the former regulations and thereupon ordered the responsible offices to revive the two dances.

units.zh: 旋屬烽火為亂，明法罔修，漢祚幾何，無暇制作。
units.en: Soon war-fires blazed again, proper law went untended, and the Later Han mandate lasted only a few years—there was no time to complete the work.
units.literal: Soon afterward war-fires arose in disorder, bright laws went unrepaired, and the Han mandate lasted but briefly, with no leisure for composition.

units.zh: 周顯德五年冬，將立歲仗，有司以崇牙樹羽，宿設於殿庭。
units.en: In the winter of the fifth year of Xiande under the Zhou, as the year-end guard ceremony was being prepared, the responsible offices erected lofty frames with plumes and set them up overnight in the palace courtyard.
units.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Xiande of Zhou, when the year-end guard ceremony was to be established, the responsible offices set up lofty teeth and planted feathers overnight in the palace courtyard.

units.zh: 世宗因親臨樂懸，試其聲奏，見鐘磬之類，有設而不擊者，訊於工師，皆不能對。
units.en: Shizong went in person to inspect the suspended instruments and test their sound. He found bells and chimes set out but left unplayed, and when he questioned the craftsmen, none could explain why.
units.literal: Shizong thereupon personally inspected the suspended music, tested its sound and performance, and saw that among bells, chimes, and the like some were set up but not struck; he questioned the craftsmen, and none could answer.

units.zh: 世宗惻然，乃命翰林學士、判太常寺事竇儼參詳其制，又命樞密使王樸考正其聲。
units.en: Deeply troubled, Shizong ordered the Hanlin academician and acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Dou Yan, to review the regulations in detail, and the Privy Council commissioner Wang Pu to correct the pitches.
units.literal: Shizong was moved with concern and thereupon ordered Hanlin academician and acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dou Yan to examine the regulations in detail, and also ordered Privy Council commissioner Wang Pu to correct the pitches.

units.zh: 樸乃用古累黍之法，以審其度，造成律準，其狀如琴而巨，凡設十三弦以定六律、六呂旋相為宮之義。
units.en: Pu applied the ancient method of stacking millet grains to determine the measures and built a pitch standard shaped like an oversized zither, with thirteen strings arranged to establish the six lü and six lü alternately generating the tonic.
units.literal: Pu then used the ancient method of stacking millet grains to determine the measures, and constructed a pitch standard shaped like a large zither, setting thirteen strings in all to fix the meaning of the six lü and six lü alternately generating the tonic.

units.zh: 世宗善之，申命百官議而行之。
units.en: Shizong approved the design and directed all officials to deliberate and put it into effect.
units.literal: Shizong approved it and ordered all officials to deliberate and put it into practice.

units.zh: 今亦備紀於後，以誌五代雅樂沿革之由焉。
units.en: What follows records these matters in full, tracing how elegant music evolved through the Five Dynasties.
units.literal: Now these are also fully recorded below, to mark the reasons for the evolution of elegant music in the Five Dynasties.

units.zh: 梁開平初，太祖受禪，始建宗廟，凡四室，每室有登歌、酌獻之舞：肅祖宣元皇帝室曰《大合之舞》。
units.en: Early in Kaiping of the Liang, when Taizu accepted the abdication, he established the ancestral temple with four chambers. Each chamber had dances for the ascending song and the libation offering: the chamber of Sole Ancestor Emperor Xuan Yuan used the Dance of Great Harmony.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping of Liang, when Taizu received the abdication, he first established the ancestral temple, four chambers in all; each chamber had dances for ascending song and libation offering: the chamber of Sole Ancestor Emperor Xuan Yuan was called the Dance of Great Harmony.

units.zh: 敬祖光憲皇帝室曰《象功之舞》。
units.en: The chamber of Revered Ancestor Emperor Guang Xian used the Dance of Symbolizing Merit.
units.literal: The chamber of Revered Ancestor Emperor Guang Xian was called the Dance of Symbolizing Merit.

units.zh: 憲祖昭武皇帝室曰《來儀之舞》。
units.en: The chamber of Ancestor of the Constitution Emperor Zhao Wu used the Dance of Coming Rites.
units.literal: The chamber of Ancestor of the Constitution Emperor Zhao Wu was called the Dance of Coming Rites.

units.zh: 烈祖文穆皇帝室曰《昭德之舞》。
units.en: The chamber of Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Wen Mu used the Dance of Manifest Virtue.
units.literal: The chamber of Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Wen Mu was called the Dance of Manifest Virtue.

units.zh: 二年春，梁祖將議郊禋，有司撰進樂名、舞名：樂曰《慶和之樂》。
units.en: In the spring of the second year, as the Liang founder prepared to discuss the suburban sacrifice, the responsible offices submitted proposed names for the music and dances: the music was to be called Music of Celebrating Harmony.
units.literal: In the spring of the second year, when the Liang founder was about to deliberate on suburban sacrifice, the responsible offices drafted and presented music names and dance names: the music was called Music of Celebrating Harmony.

units.zh: 舞曰《崇德之舞》。
units.en: The dance was to be called the Dance of Honoring Virtue.
units.literal: The dance was called the Dance of Honoring Virtue.

units.zh: 皇帝行奏《慶順》。
units.en: When the emperor processed, Celebrating Compliance was played.
units.literal: When the emperor processed, they played Celebrating Compliance.

units.zh: 奠玉帛登歌奏《慶平》。
units.en: At the offering of jade and silk, the ascending song Celebrating Peace was performed.
units.literal: At the offering of jade and silk, the ascending song played Celebrating Peace.

units.zh: 迎俎奏《慶肅》。
units.en: When the sacrificial stands were brought forward, Celebrating Solemnity was played.
units.literal: At receiving the sacrificial stands, they played Celebrating Solemnity.

units.zh: 酌獻奏《慶熙》。
units.en: At the libation offering, Celebrating Radiance was played.
units.literal: At the libation offering, they played Celebrating Radiance.

units.zh: 飲福酒奏《慶隆》。
units.en: At drinking the blessing wine, Celebrating Abundance was played.
units.literal: At drinking the blessing wine, they played Celebrating Abundance.

units.zh: 送文舞迎武舞奏《慶融》。
units.en: When the civil dance departed and the military dance entered, Celebrating Fusion was played.
units.literal: At sending off the civil dance and receiving the military dance, they played Celebrating Fusion.

units.zh: 亞獻奏《慶和》。
units.en: At the secondary offering, Celebrating Harmony was played.
units.literal: At the secondary offering, they played Celebrating Harmony.

units.zh: 終獻奏《慶休》。
units.en: At the final offering, Celebrating Rest was played.
units.literal: At the final offering, they played Celebrating Rest.

units.zh: 樂章各一首。

units.zh: 太廟迎神，舞名《開平》。

units.en: Music was performed for the emperor's procession, hand-washing, ascending song, drinking the blessing wine, removal of the vessels, and sending off the spirits.

units.en: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Tianfu under Jin, the ritual officials memorialized: "For next year's New Year's Day, when the princes and dukes offer birthday felicitations and the emperor raises his cup, Music of Primal Unity should be played;
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Tianfu of Jin, the ritual officials memorialized: "Next year's New Year's Day, when the princes and dukes offer longevity wishes and the emperor raises his cup, please perform Music of Primal Unity;

units.zh: 再舉酒，奏《文同之樂》。」
units.en: when he raises his cup a second time, Music of Cultural Unity should be played."
units.literal: when the cup is raised a second time, perform Music of Cultural Unity."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The proposal was approved.
units.literal: This was approved.

units.zh: 五年，始議重興二舞，詔曰：「正冬二節，朝會舊儀，廢於離亂之時，興自和平之代。
units.en: In the fifth year, deliberations began on reviving the two dances. An edict declared: "The two mid-winter festivals and the court assembly rites of old were abandoned in times of turmoil and are to be restored in an age of peace.
units.literal: In the fifth year, they first deliberated on reviving the two dances. An edict stated: "The two mid-winter festivals and the court assembly rites of old were abandoned in times of disorder and are to be revived in an age of peace.

units.zh: 將期備物，全系用心；
units.en: We expect every implement to be prepared in full, and that depends entirely on devoted effort;
units.literal: We expect to prepare the implements in full, which depends entirely on devoted effort;

units.zh: 須議擇人，同為定制。
units.en: we must deliberate and choose the right men to establish these regulations together.
units.literal: we must deliberate and select personnel to establish these regulations together.

units.zh: 其正冬朝會禮節、樂章、二舞行列等事宜，差太常卿崔棁、御史中丞竇貞固、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允與太常寺官一一詳定。
units.en: Concerning the mid-winter court assembly ritual procedures, hymns, formations of the two dances, and related matters, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Zhi, Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices are commissioned to determine each point in detail.
units.literal: As for the mid-winter court assembly ritual procedures, hymns, formations of the two dances, and related matters, commission Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Zhi, Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, together with officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to determine each in detail.

units.zh: 禮從新意，道在舊章，庶知治世之和，漸見移風之善。」
units.en: Ritual may take on new forms, but the Way lies in the old regulations; we hope thereby to manifest the harmony of a well-governed age and gradually to see customs transformed for the better."
units.literal: Ritual may follow new intentions, but the Way lies in the old regulations; we hope thereby to know the harmony of a well-governed age and gradually see the goodness of transforming customs."

units.zh: 其年秋，棁等具述制度上奏云：
units.en: That autumn, Zhi and his colleagues submitted a full account of the regulations, stating:
units.literal: That autumn, Zhi and the others fully set forth the regulations and memorialized, stating:

units.zh: 案《禮》云：「天子以德為車，以樂為禦。」
units.en: According to the Rites: "The Son of Heaven takes virtue as his chariot and music as his driver."
units.literal: According to the Rites: "The Son of Heaven takes virtue as his chariot and music as his driver."

units.zh: 「大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。」
units.en: "Great music harmonizes with Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares the seasons with Heaven and Earth."
units.literal: "Great music harmonizes with Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares the seasons with Heaven and Earth."

units.zh: 又曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮；
units.en: It also says: "In securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual;
units.literal: It also says: "In securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual;

units.zh: 移風易俗，莫善於樂。」
units.en: in transforming customs and changing habits, nothing is better than music."
units.literal: in transforming customs and changing habits, nothing is better than music."

units.zh: 故樂書議舞云：夫樂在耳曰聲，在目曰容。
units.en: Therefore the Treatise on Music, in its discussion of dance, states: What the ear receives is called sound; what the eye beholds is called form.
units.literal: Therefore the Treatise on Music discussing dance states: What is in the ear is called sound; what is before the eye is called form.

units.zh: 聲應乎耳，可以聽知；
units.en: Sound answers to the ear and can be known by hearing;
units.literal: Sound responds to the ear and can be known by hearing;

units.zh: 容藏於心，難以貌睹。
units.en: form is stored in the heart and cannot easily be seen in outward appearance.
units.literal: form is stored in the heart and is difficult to behold in appearance.

units.zh: 故聖人假幹戚羽旄以表其容，發揚蹈厲以見其意，聲容和合，則大樂備矣。
units.en: Therefore the sages borrowed shields, axes, feathers, and banners to manifest form, and through vigorous stamping displayed intent; when sound and form were united, great music was complete.
units.literal: Therefore the sages borrowed shields, axes, feathers, and banners to manifest their form, and through vigorous stamping displayed their intent; when sound and form were united, great music was complete.

units.zh: 又案《義鏡》，問鼓吹十二案合於何所？
units.en: We further examined the Mirror of Rites and asked: To what institution do the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion correspond?
units.literal: We further examined the Mirror of Rites and asked: To what do the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion music correspond?

units.zh: 答云：《周禮》鼓人掌六鼓四金，漢朝乃有黃門鼓吹。
units.en: The answer states: In the Rites of Zhou the drum master supervised six drums and four metal instruments; under the Han there was the Yellow Gate wind-and-percussion ensemble.
units.literal: The answer states: In the Rites of Zhou the drum master supervised six drums and four metal instruments; the Han dynasty then had the Yellow Gate wind-and-percussion.

units.zh: 崔豹《古今註》云：因張騫使西域，得《摩訶兜勒》一曲，李延年增之，分為二十八曲。
units.en: Cui Bao's Notes Ancient and Modern states: When Zhang Qian was sent to the Western Regions, he brought back a piece called Mahadoule; Li Yannian expanded it and divided it into twenty-eight pieces.
units.literal: Cui Bao's Notes Ancient and Modern states: Because Zhang Qian was sent to the Western Regions, he obtained one piece called Mahadoule; Li Yannian expanded it and divided it into twenty-eight pieces.

units.zh: 梁置鼓吹清商令二人。
units.en: The Liang established two directors of wind-and-percussion and pure shang music.
units.literal: Liang established two directors of wind-and-percussion and pure shang music.

units.zh: 唐又有堈鼓、金鉦、大鼓、長鳴、歌簫、笳、笛，合為鼓吹十二案，大享會則設於懸外。
units.en: The Tang added mounted drums, golden chimes, great drums, long horns, singing pipes, reed pipes, and flutes, combined into twelve sets of wind-and-percussion; at great feasts they were placed outside the suspended bells and chimes.
units.literal: Tang further had mounted drums, golden chimes, great drums, long horns, singing pipes, reed pipes, and flutes, combined into twelve sets of wind-and-percussion; at great feasts they were set outside the suspended instruments.

units.zh: 此乃是設二舞及鼓吹十二案之由也。
units.en: This is the origin of establishing the two dances and the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion.
units.literal: This is the reason for establishing the two dances and the twelve sets of wind-and-percussion.

units.zh: 今議一從令式，排列教習。
units.en: We now propose to follow the current regulations in full and arrange instruction in formation.
units.literal: Now we propose to follow the current regulations entirely and arrange training in formation.

units.zh: 文舞郎六十四人，分為八佾，每佾八人。
units.en: There are sixty-four civil dancers, divided into eight rows of eight men each.
units.literal: Sixty-four civil dancers, divided into eight rows of eight men each.

units.zh: 左手執籥。
units.en: Each holds a yue flute in his left hand.
units.literal: In the left hand they hold the yue flute.

units.zh: 《禮》云：「葦籥，伊耆氏之樂也。」
units.en: The Rites states: "The reed yue was the music of the Yixi clan."
units.literal: The Rites states: "The reed yue was the music of the Yixi clan."

units.zh: 《周禮》有「籥師教國子」，《爾雅》曰：籥如笛，三孔而短，大者七孔，謂之簅。
units.en: The Rites of Zhou records that "the yue master teaches the sons of the state"; the Erya says: the yue resembles a flute, with three holes and short in form; the larger kind has seven holes and is called chan.
units.literal: The Rites of Zhou has "the yue master teaches the sons of the state"; the Erya says: the yue is like a flute, with three holes and short; the larger kind has seven holes and is called chan.

units.zh: 歷代已來，文舞所用，凡用籥六十有四。
units.en: From age to age, the civil dance has used sixty-four yue flutes in all.
units.literal: From successive ages onward, what the civil dance has used—in all, sixty-four yue flutes are employed.

units.zh: 右手執翟，《周禮》所謂羽舞也。
units.en: In the right hand they hold the di plume—what the Rites of Zhou calls the feather dance.
units.literal: In the right hand they hold the di plume; this is what the Rites of Zhou calls the feather dance.

units.zh: 《書》云：「舞幹羽於兩階。」
units.en: The Documents states: "They danced with shields and plumes on the two flights of steps."
units.literal: The Documents states: "They danced with shields and plumes on the two flights of steps."

units.zh: 翟，山雉也，以雉羽公析連攢而為之。
units.en: The di is a mountain pheasant; it is fashioned by evenly splitting and bundling pheasant feathers together.
units.literal: The di is a mountain pheasant; it is made by evenly splitting and bundling pheasant feathers together.

units.zh: 二人執纛前引，數於舞人之外。
units.en: Two men hold battle standards and lead in front, stationed outside the dancers.
units.literal: Two men hold battle standards and lead in front, positioned outside the dancers.

units.zh: 舞人冠進賢冠，服黃紗袍，白紗中單，皂領褾，白練𧞔襠，白布大口袴，革帶，烏皮履，白布襪。
units.en: The dancers wear the forward-virtue cap, yellow gauze robes, white gauze undergarments, black collars with ties, white silk overskirt panels, white cloth wide-legged trousers, leather belts, black leather shoes, and white cloth socks.
units.literal: The dancers wear the forward-virtue cap, yellow gauze robes, white gauze undergarments, black collars with ties, white silk overskirt panels, white cloth wide-legged trousers, leather belts, black leather shoes, and white cloth socks.

units.zh: 武舞郎六十四人，分為八佾。
units.en: There are sixty-four military dancers, divided into eight rows of eight.
units.literal: Sixty-four military dancers, divided into eight rows of eight.

units.zh: 左手執幹。
units.en: Each holds a shield in his left hand.
units.literal: In the left hand they hold the shield.

units.zh: 幹，楯也，今之旁牌，所以翳身也，其色赤，中畫獸形，故謂之朱幹。
units.en: The gan is a shield—what are now called side-boards—used to screen the body. They are red, with beast forms painted at the center, and are therefore called vermilion shields.
units.literal: The gan is a shield—what are now called side-boards—used to screen the body; their color is red, with beast forms painted in the center, hence they are called vermilion shields.

units.zh: 《周禮》所謂兵舞，取其武象，用楯六十有四。
units.en: This is what the Rites of Zhou calls the military dance, taking its martial imagery; sixty-four shields are employed.
units.literal: This is what the Rites of Zhou calls the military dance, taking its martial imagery; sixty-four shields are used.

units.zh: 右手執戚。
units.en: Each holds a battle-axe in his right hand.
units.literal: In the right hand they hold the battle-axe.

units.zh: 戚，斧也，上飾以玉，故謂之玉戚。
units.en: The qi is an axe, adorned with jade at the top, and is therefore called the jade qi.
units.literal: The qi is an axe, adorned with jade on top, hence it is called the jade qi.

units.zh: 二人執旌前引，旌似旗而小，絳色，畫升龍。
units.en: Two men hold pennants and lead in front. Pennants resemble flags but are smaller, crimson in color, and painted with ascending dragons.
units.literal: Two men hold pennants and lead in front; pennants resemble flags but are smaller, crimson in color, painted with ascending dragons.

units.zh: 二人執鼗鼓，二人執鐸。
units.en: Two men hold hand drums, and two men hold clapper bells.
units.literal: Two men hold hand drums, two men hold clapper bells.

units.zh: 《周禮》有四金之奏，其三曰金鐸，以通鼓，形如大鈴，仰而振之。
units.en: The Rites of Zhou describes the playing of the four metals; the third is the metal duo, used to signal the drum. Shaped like a large bell, it is shaken face upward.
units.literal: The Rites of Zhou has the playing of the four metals; the third is called the metal duo, used to signal the drum; shaped like a large bell, it is shaken face upward.

units.zh: 金錞二，每錞二人舉之，一人奏之。
units.en: There are two metal chuns; for each chun two men lift it and one man strikes it.
units.literal: Two metal chuns; for each chun two men lift it, one man strikes it.

units.zh: 《周禮》四金之奏，一曰金錞，以和鼓，銅鑄為之，其色黑，其形圓，若椎，上大下小，高三尺六寸有六分，圍二尺四寸，上有伏虎之狀，旁有耳，獸形銜镮。
units.en: In the Rites of Zhou's four metals, the first is the metal chun, used to harmonize with the drum. Cast in bronze, it is black and round like a mallet, large at the top and small at the bottom, three chi six cun and six fen high and two chi four cun around, with a crouching tiger on top, ears at the sides, and beast-shaped ring handles.
units.literal: In the Rites of Zhou's four metals, the first is the metal chun, used to harmonize with the drum; cast in bronze, its color is black, its shape round like a mallet, large at the top and small at the bottom, three chi six cun and six fen in height, two chi four cun in circumference, with the form of a crouching tiger on top, ears at the sides, and beast-shaped ring handles.

units.zh: 二人執鐃以次之。
units.en: Two men hold nao bells and follow next.
units.literal: Two men hold nao bells to follow next.

units.zh: 《周禮》四金之奏，二曰金鐃，以止鼓，如鈴無舌，搖柄以鳴之。
units.en: In the Rites of Zhou's four metals, the second is the metal nao, used to stop the drum. Like a bell without a clapper, it is sounded by shaking the handle.
units.literal: In the Rites of Zhou's four metals, the second is the metal nao, used to stop the drum; like a bell without a clapper, it is rung by shaking the handle.

units.zh: 二人掌相在左，《禮》云：「治亂以相。」
units.en: Two men hold the xiang on the left. The Rites states: "To govern chaos and order with the xiang."
units.literal: Two men hold the xiang on the left; the Rites states: "To govern chaos and order with the xiang."

units.zh: 制如小鼓，用皮為表，實之以糠，撫之以節樂。
units.en: It is made like a small drum, with hide as the outer layer, filled with chaff, and patted to mark the rhythm of the music.
units.literal: Made like a small drum, with hide as the outer layer, filled with chaff, and patted to mark the rhythm of the music.

units.zh: 二人掌雅在右，《禮》云：「訊疾以雅。」
units.en: Two men hold the ya on the right. The Rites states: "To report speed with the ya."
units.literal: Two men hold the ya on the right; the Rites states: "To report speed with the ya."

units.zh: 以木為之，狀如漆筒而弇口，大二尺圍，長五尺六寸，以羖皮鞔之，旁有二紐，髹畫，賓醉而出，以器築地，明行不失節。
units.en: It is made of wood, shaped like a lacquered tube with a closed mouth, two chi around and five chi six cun long, covered with ram hide, with two loops at the sides and lacquer decoration. When the guest, drunk, goes out, the instrument is used to beat the ground, making clear that the procession does not lose its measure.
units.literal: Made of wood, shaped like a lacquered tube with a closed mouth, two chi in circumference, five chi six cun in length, covered with ram hide, with two loops at the sides and lacquer decoration; when the guest, drunk, goes out, the instrument is used to beat the ground, making clear that the procession does not lose its measure.

units.zh: 武舞人服弁，平巾幘，金支緋絲大袖，緋絲布裲襠，甲金飾，白練𧞔襠，錦騰蛇起梁帶，豹文大口布袴，烏皮靴。
units.en: Military dancers wear caps, plain kerchiefs, gold-mounted crimson silk large sleeves, crimson silk doublet panels, gold-trimmed armor ornaments, white silk overskirt panels, brocade belts with rising snake patterns, leopard-pattern wide-legged cloth trousers, and black leather boots.
units.literal: Military dancers wear caps, plain kerchiefs, gold-mounted crimson silk large sleeves, crimson silk doublet panels, gold-trimmed armor ornaments, white silk overskirt panels, brocade belts with rising snake patterns, leopard-pattern wide-legged cloth trousers, and black leather boots.

units.zh: 工人二十，數於舞人之外。
units.en: Twenty artisans are stationed outside the dancers.
units.literal: Twenty artisans, positioned outside the dancers.

units.zh: 武弁朱翙，革帶，烏皮履，白練𧞔襠，白布襪。
units.en: They wear martial caps with vermilion pheasant tails, leather belts, black leather shoes, white silk overskirt panels, and white cloth socks.
units.literal: They wear martial caps with vermilion pheasant tails, leather belts, black leather shoes, white silk overskirt panels, and white cloth socks.

units.zh: 殿庭仍加鼓吹十二案。
units.en: In the palace courtyard, twelve sets of wind-and-percussion are additionally installed.
units.literal: In the palace courtyard twelve sets of wind-and-percussion are additionally installed.

units.zh: 《義鏡》云：常設氈案，以氈為床也。
units.en: The Mirror of Rites states that felt platforms are regularly set up, with felt serving as the base.
units.literal: The Mirror of Rites states: Felt platforms are regularly set up, with felt serving as the base.

units.zh: 今請制大床十二，慶容九人，振作歌樂，其床為熊羆貙豹騰倚之狀以承之，象百獸率舞之意。
units.en: We now request that twelve large platforms be made, each accommodating nine performers, to rouse singing and music. The platforms should be shaped as bears, brown bears, leopards, and wildcats rearing and leaning to support them, symbolizing the hundred beasts leading the dance.
units.literal: Now we request that twelve large platforms be made, each accommodating nine performers, to rouse singing and music; the platforms should be shaped as bears, brown bears, leopards, and wildcats rearing and leaning to support them, symbolizing the hundred beasts leading the dance.

units.zh: 分置於建鼓之外，各三案，每案羽葆鼓一，大鼓一，金錞一，歌二人，簫二人，笳二人。
units.en: They are placed separately outside the mounted drums, three sets to each side. Each set has one feathered-canopy drum, one great drum, one metal chun, two singers, two pipe players, and two reed-pipe players.
units.literal: Placed separately outside the mounted drums, three sets each; each set has one feathered-canopy drum, one great drum, one metal chun, two singers, two pipe players, and two reed-pipe players.

units.zh: 十二案，樂工百有八人，舞郎一百三十有二人，取年十五已上，弱冠已下，容止端正者。
units.en: For the twelve sets there are one hundred eight musicians and one hundred thirty-two dancers, selected from those fifteen years of age or above and not yet come of age, with upright bearing and deportment.
units.literal: For the twelve sets: one hundred eight musicians and one hundred thirty-two dancers, selected from those fifteen years old or above and not yet come of age, with upright bearing and deportment.

units.zh: 其歌曲名號、樂章詞句，中書條奏，差官修撰。
units.en: As for the song titles, music names, and lyrics, the Secretariat will itemize and submit them, and officials will be dispatched to compose them.
units.literal: As for the song titles, music names, and lyrics, the Secretariat will itemize and submit them, and officials will be dispatched to compose them.

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The request was approved.
units.literal: Approved.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·崔棁傳》：高祖詔太常復文武二舞，詳定正冬朝會禮及樂章。
units.en: (Ouyang's History [New History of the Five Dynasties], Biography of Cui Zhuo: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
units.literal: (Ouyang's History, Biography of Cui Zhuo: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.

units.zh: 自唐末之亂，禮樂制度亡失已久，棁與御史中丞竇貞固、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允等草定之。
units.en: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost. Zhuo, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others, drafted regulations for them.
units.literal: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zhuo together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others drafted regulations for them.

units.zh: 其年冬至，高祖會朝崇元殿，廷設宮懸，二舞在北，登歌在上。
units.en: That year at the winter solstice, Gaozu held court at Chongyuan Hall. Court suspended bells and chimes were set up in the hall, with the two dances to the north and ascending song above.
units.literal: That year at the winter solstice, Gaozu held court at Chongyuan Hall; court suspended bells and chimes were set up in the hall, the two dances to the north, ascending song above.

units.zh: 文舞郎八佾六十有四人，冠進賢。
units.en: Sixty-four civil dancers in eight rows wore the forward-virtue cap.
units.literal: Sixty-four civil dancers in eight rows, wearing the forward-virtue cap.

units.zh: 黃紗袍，白中單，白練𧞔襠，白布大口袴，革帶履，左執枿，右秉翟，執纛引者二人。
units.en: They wore yellow gauze robes, white undergarments, white silk overskirt panels, white cloth wide-legged trousers, leather belts and shoes; in the left hand they held the yue flute, in the right they grasped plumes, and two men holding battle standards led.
units.literal: Yellow gauze robes, white undergarments, white silk overskirt panels, white cloth wide-legged trousers, leather belts and shoes; in the left hand they hold the yue flute, in the right they grasp plumes; two men holding battle standards lead.

units.zh: 武舞郎八佾六十有四人，服平巾幘，緋絲布大袖繡襠，甲金飾，白練𧞔襠，錦騰蛇起梁帶，豹文大口袴，烏靴，左執幹，右執戚，執旌引者二人。
units.en: Sixty-four military dancers in eight rows wore plain kerchiefs, crimson silk large sleeves with embroidered panels, gold-trimmed armor ornaments, white silk overskirt panels, brocade belts with rising snake patterns, leopard-pattern wide-legged trousers, and black boots. In the left hand they held shields, in the right battle-axes, and two men holding pennants led.
units.literal: Sixty-four military dancers in eight rows wore plain kerchiefs, crimson silk large sleeves with embroidered panels, gold-trimmed armor ornaments, white silk overskirt panels, brocade belts with rising snake patterns, leopard-pattern wide-legged trousers, and black boots; in the left hand they held shields, in the right battle-axes; two men holding pennants led.

units.zh: 加鼓吹十二案，負以熊豹，以象百獸率舞。
units.en: Twelve sets of wind-and-percussion were added, borne on bear and leopard figures, to symbolize the hundred beasts leading the dance.
units.literal: Twelve sets of wind-and-percussion were added, borne on bear and leopard figures, to symbolize the hundred beasts leading the dance.

units.zh: 案設羽葆鼓一，大鼓一，金錞一，歌簫、笳各二人。
units.en: Each set had one feathered-canopy drum, one great drum, one metal chun, and two each for singing pipes and reed pipes.
units.literal: Each set had one feathered-canopy drum, one great drum, one metal chun, and two each for singing pipes and reed pipes.

units.zh: 王公上壽，天子舉爵，奏《元同》；
units.en: When princes and nobles offered longevity wishes, the Son of Heaven raised his cup and they played "Primary Unity";
units.literal: When princes and nobles offered longevity wishes, the Son of Heaven raised his cup and they played "Primary Unity";

units.zh: 二舉，登歌奏《文同》；
units.en: At the second raising, ascending song played "Literary Unity";
units.literal: At the second raising, ascending song played "Literary Unity";

units.zh: 舉食，文舞《昭德》，武舞《成功》之曲。
units.en: When food was served, the civil dance played "Manifest Virtue" and the military dance the piece "Accomplishment."
units.literal: When food was served, the civil dance played "Manifest Virtue" and the military dance the piece "Accomplishment."

units.zh: 禮畢，高祖大悅，賜棁金帛，群臣左右睹者皆贊嘆之。
units.en: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhuo. All the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
units.literal: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhuo; all the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.

units.zh: 然禮樂廢久，而制作簡繆，又繼以龜茲部《霓裳法曲》，參亂雅音。
units.en: Yet ritual and music had long been abandoned, and what was made was simple and flawed. Moreover they added the Kucha section's "Rainbow Skirt Law Piece," mingling and disrupting elegant music.
units.literal: Yet ritual and music had been abandoned for long, and what was made was simple and flawed; moreover they added the Kucha section's "Rainbow Skirt Law Piece," mingling and disrupting elegant music.

units.zh: 其樂工舞郎，多教坊伶人、百工商賈、州縣避役之人，又無老師良工教習。
units.en: The musicians and dancers were mostly entertainment-bureau performers, artisans and merchants, and people evading corvée duty from prefectures and districts. Moreover there were no veteran masters or skilled craftsmen to teach them.
units.literal: The musicians and dancers were mostly entertainment-bureau performers, artisans and merchants, and people evading corvée duty from prefectures and districts; moreover there were no veteran masters or skilled craftsmen to teach them.

units.zh: 明年正旦，復奏於庭，而登歌發聲，悲離煩慝，如《薤露》、《虞殯》之音，舞者行列進退，皆不應節，聞者皆悲憤。
units.en: The next year at New Year's Day they again performed in court, but when ascending song sounded it was mournful, troubled, and grievous, like the tones of "Wild Leek Dew" and "Yu Funereal." The dancers' ranks advancing and retreating all failed to match the beat, and all who heard it felt grief and anger.
units.literal: The next year at New Year's Day they again performed in court, but when ascending song sounded it was mournful, troubled, and grievous, like the tones of "Wild Leek Dew" and "Yu Funereal"; the dancers' ranks advancing and retreating all failed to match the beat; all who heard it felt grief and anger.

units.zh: 開運二年，太常少卿陶穀奏廢二舞。）〉
units.en: In the second year of Kaiyun, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tao Gu memorialized to abolish the two dances.)〉
units.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tao Gu memorialized to abolish the two dances.)〉

units.zh: 漢高祖受命之年，秋九月，權太常卿張昭上疏，奏改一代樂名，其略曰？
units.en: In the year when Han Gaozu received the Mandate, in the ninth month of autumn, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial requesting changes to the music names of the dynasty. Stated in summary:
units.literal: In the year when Han Gaozu received the Mandate, in the ninth month of autumn, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial requesting changes to the music names of the dynasty; stated in summary:

units.zh: 昔周公相成王，制禮作樂，殿庭遍奏六代舞，所謂《雲門》、《大咸》、《大韶》、《大夏》、《大》、《大武》也。
units.en: Formerly, when the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, he established rites and made music. In the palace hall the dances of the six ages were performed throughout—those called "Gate of Clouds," "Great All-Pervading," "Great Shao," "Great Xia," "Great Yin," and "Great Martial."
units.literal: Formerly when the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, he established rites and made music; in the palace hall the dances of the six ages were performed throughout—those called "Gate of Clouds," "Great All-Pervading," "Great Shao," "Great Xia," "Great Yin," and "Great Martial."

units.zh: 周室既衰，王綱不振，諸樂多廢，惟《大韶》、《大武》二曲存焉。
units.en: When the Zhou house declined and royal discipline no longer held, most music was abandoned. Only the two pieces "Great Shao" and "Great Martial" remained.
units.literal: When the Zhou house declined and royal discipline no longer held, most music was abandoned; only the two pieces "Great Shao" and "Great Martial" remained.

units.zh: 秦、漢以來，名為二舞：文舞，《韶》也；
units.en: From Qin and Han onward they were named the two dances: the civil dance was Shao;
units.literal: From Qin and Han onward they were named the two dances: the civil dance was Shao;

units.zh: 武舞，《武》也。
units.en: the military dance was Wu.
units.literal: the military dance was Wu.

units.zh: 漢時改為《文始》、《五行之舞》，歷代因而不改。
units.en: In Han times they were changed to "Literary Beginning" and "Dance of the Five Phases," and successive dynasties followed without change.
units.literal: In Han times they were changed to "Literary Beginning" and "Dance of the Five Phases"; successive dynasties followed without change.

units.zh: 貞觀作樂之時，祖孝孫改隋文舞為《治康之舞》武舞為《凱安之舞》。
units.en: When music was composed in the Zhenguan era, Zu Xiaosun changed the Sui civil dance to "Dance of Governing Tranquility" and the military dance to "Dance of Victorious Peace."
units.literal: When music was composed in the Zhenguan era, Zu Xiaosun changed the Sui civil dance to "Dance of Governing Tranquility" and the military dance to "Dance of Victorious Peace."

units.zh: 貞觀中，有《秦王破陣樂》、《功成慶善樂》二舞，樂府又用為二舞，是舞有四焉。
units.en: In the Zhenguan era there were two dances, "Prince of Qin's Breaking the Battle Line" and "Celebrating Goodness upon Accomplishment." The Music Bureau also employed them as two dances, so there were four dances in all.
units.literal: In the Zhenguan era there were two dances, "Prince of Qin's Breaking the Battle Line" and "Celebrating Goodness upon Accomplishment"; the Music Bureau also employed them as two dances—thus there were four dances.

units.zh: 前朝行用年深，不可遽廢，俟國家偃伯靈臺，即別召工師，更其節奏，今改其名，具書如左：祖孝孫所定二舞名，文舞曰《治康之舞》，請改《治安之舞》；
units.en: The former dynasty's usage has run deep over many years and cannot be abruptly abolished. When the state rests its weapons and the Spirit Terrace is at peace, skilled craftsmen will be summoned separately to revise their rhythms. For now their names are changed, fully recorded as follows: the two dances fixed by Zu Xiaosun—the civil dance called "Dance of Governing Tranquility"—please change to "Dance of Governing Peace";
units.literal: The former dynasty's usage has run deep over the years and cannot be abruptly abolished; when the state rests its weapons and the Spirit Terrace is at peace, skilled craftsmen will be summoned separately to revise their rhythms. For now their names are changed, fully recorded as follows: the two dances fixed by Zu Xiaosun—the civil dance called "Dance of Governing Tranquility," please change to "Dance of Governing Peace";

units.zh: 武舞曰《凱安之舞》，請改為《振德之舞》。
units.en: the military dance called "Dance of Victorious Peace"—please change to "Dance of Shaking Virtue."
units.literal: the military dance called "Dance of Victorious Peace," please change to "Dance of Shaking Virtue."

units.zh: 貞觀中二舞名，文舞《功成慶善樂》，前朝名《九功舞》，請改為《觀象之舞》；
units.en: The two dance names of the Zhenguan era: the civil dance "Celebrating Goodness upon Accomplishment," formerly called "Dance of the Nine Achievements" in the previous dynasty—please change to "Dance of Observing the Images";
units.literal: The two dance names of the Zhenguan era: the civil dance "Celebrating Goodness upon Accomplishment," formerly called "Dance of the Nine Achievements" in the previous dynasty, please change to "Dance of Observing the Images";

units.zh: 武舞《秦王破陣樂》，前朝名為《七德舞》，請改為《講功之舞》。
units.en: the military dance "Prince of Qin's Breaking the Battle Line," formerly called "Dance of the Seven Virtues" in the previous dynasty—please change to "Dance of Expounding Merit."
units.literal: the military dance "Prince of Qin's Breaking the Battle Line," formerly called "Dance of the Seven Virtues" in the previous dynasty, please change to "Dance of Expounding Merit."

units.zh: 其《治安》、《振德》二舞，請依舊郊廟行用，以文舞降神，武舞送神。
units.en: As for the two dances "Governing Peace" and "Shaking Virtue," please continue to use them as before at suburban and temple rites, with the civil dance for welcoming the spirits and the military dance for sending them off.
units.literal: As for the two dances "Governing Peace" and "Shaking Virtue," please continue to use them as before at suburban and temple rites, with the civil dance for welcoming the spirits and the military dance for sending them off.

units.zh: 其《觀象》、《講功》二舞，請依舊宴會行用。
units.en: As for the two dances "Observing the Images" and "Expounding Merit," please continue to use them as before at banquets.
units.literal: As for the two dances "Observing the Images" and "Expounding Merit," please continue to use them as before at banquets.

units.zh: 又請改《十二和樂》云：
units.en: He further requested changes to the "Twelve Harmonious Pieces," stating:
units.literal: He further requested changes to the "Twelve Harmonious Pieces," stating:

units.zh: 昔周朝奏六代之樂，即今二舞之類是也。
units.en: Formerly the Zhou court played the music of the six ages—the same kind as today's two dances.
units.literal: Formerly the Zhou court played the music of the six ages—this is the same kind as today's two dances.

units.zh: 其賓祭常用，別有《九夏之樂》，即《肆夏》、《皇夏》等是也，梁武帝善音樂，改《九夏》為《十二雅》，前朝祖孝孫改雅為和，示不相沿也。
units.en: For guest rites and sacrifices in common use there were separately the "Nine Summers Pieces," such as "Free Summer" and "August Summer." Emperor Wu of Liang was skilled in music and changed the "Nine Summers" to the "Twelve Elegances." In the previous dynasty Zu Xiaosun changed elegance to harmony, showing that one should not simply follow precedent.
units.literal: For guest rites and sacrifices in common use there were separately the "Nine Summers Pieces," such as "Free Summer" and "August Summer"; Emperor Wu of Liang was skilled in music and changed the "Nine Summers" to the "Twelve Elegances"; in the previous dynasty Zu Xiaosun changed elegance to harmony, showing that one should not simply follow precedent.

units.zh: 臣今改和為成，取《韶》樂九成之義也。
units.en: Your subject now changes harmony to accomplishment, taking the meaning of the nine accomplishments of Shao music.
units.literal: Your subject now changes harmony to accomplishment, taking the meaning of the nine accomplishments of Shao music.

units.zh: 《十二成樂曲》名：祭天神奏《豫和之樂》，請改為《禋成》；
units.en: Names of the "Twelve Accomplishment Pieces": for sacrificing to Heaven they play "Music of Forethought and Harmony"—please change to "Accomplishment of the Smoke Offering";
units.literal: Names of the "Twelve Accomplishment Pieces": for sacrificing to Heaven they play "Music of Forethought and Harmony," please change to "Accomplishment of the Smoke Offering";

units.zh: 祭地祇奏《順和》，請改為《順成》；
units.en: for sacrificing to earthly spirits they play "Compliance and Harmony"—please change to "Compliance Accomplished";
units.literal: for sacrificing to earthly spirits they play "Compliance and Harmony," please change to "Compliance Accomplished";

units.zh: 祭宗廟奏《永和》，請改為《裕成》；
units.en: for sacrificing at the ancestral temple they play "Everlasting Harmony"—please change to "Abundant Accomplishment";
units.literal: for sacrificing at the ancestral temple they play "Everlasting Harmony," please change to "Abundant Accomplishment";

units.zh: 祭天地、宗廟，登歌奏《肅和》，請改為《肅成》；
units.en: for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and at the ancestral temple, ascending song plays "Solemn Harmony"—please change to "Solemn Accomplishment";
units.literal: for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and at the ancestral temple, ascending song plays "Solemn Harmony," please change to "Solemn Accomplishment";

units.zh: 皇帝臨軒奏《太和》，請改為《政成》；
units.en: when the emperor presides at court they play "Grand Harmony"—please change to "Government Accomplished";
units.literal: when the emperor presides at court they play "Grand Harmony," please change to "Government Accomplished";

units.zh: 王公出入奏《舒和》，請改為《弼成》；
units.en: when princes and nobles enter and leave they play "Easy Harmony"—please change to "Assisting Accomplishment";
units.literal: when princes and nobles enter and leave they play "Easy Harmony," please change to "Assisting Accomplishment";

units.zh: 皇帝食舉及飲宴奏《休和》，請改為《德成》；
units.en: when the emperor raises food and at drinking banquets they play "Restful Harmony"—please change to "Virtue Accomplished";
units.literal: when the emperor raises food and at drinking banquets they play "Restful Harmony," please change to "Virtue Accomplished";

units.zh: 皇帝受朝、皇后入宮奏《正和》，請改為《骍成》；
units.en: when the emperor receives court and the empress enters the palace they play "Correct Harmony"—please change to "Sacrificial Accomplishment";
units.literal: when the emperor receives court and the empress enters the palace they play "Correct Harmony," please change to "Sacrificial Accomplishment";

units.zh: 皇太子軒懸出入奏《承和》，請改為《允成》；
units.en: when the crown prince with suspended bells and chimes enters and leaves they play "Receiving Harmony"—please change to "Sincere Accomplishment";
units.literal: when the crown prince with suspended bells and chimes enters and leaves they play "Receiving Harmony," please change to "Sincere Accomplishment";

units.zh: 元日、冬至皇帝禮會，登歌奏《昭和》，請改為《慶成》；
units.en: at New Year's Day and the winter solstice when the emperor holds ceremonial assembly, ascending song plays "Bright Harmony"—please change to "Celebration Accomplished";
units.literal: at New Year's Day and the winter solstice when the emperor holds ceremonial assembly, ascending song plays "Bright Harmony," please change to "Celebration Accomplished";

units.zh: 郊廟俎入奏《雍和》，請改為《骍成》；
units.en: when sacrificial stands enter at suburban and temple rites they play "Harmonious Unity"—please change to "Sacrificial Accomplishment";
units.literal: when sacrificial stands enter at suburban and temple rites they play "Harmonious Unity," please change to "Sacrificial Accomplishment";

units.zh: 皇帝祭享、酌獻、讀祝文及飲福、受胙奏《壽和》，請改為《壽成》。
units.en: when the emperor sacrifices, pours the offering, reads the prayer text, drinks the blessing wine, and receives the sacrificial meat they play "Longevity Harmony"—please change to "Longevity Accomplished."
units.literal: when the emperor sacrifices, pours the offering, reads the prayer text, drinks the blessing wine, and receives the sacrificial meat they play "Longevity Harmony," please change to "Longevity Accomplished."

units.zh: 祖孝孫元定《十二和曲》，開元朝又奏三和，遂有《十五和》之名。
units.en: Zu Xiaosun originally fixed the "Twelve Harmonious Pieces." In the Kaiyuan reign three more harmonious pieces were added, and thus arose the name "Fifteen Harmonious Pieces."
units.literal: Zu Xiaosun originally fixed the "Twelve Harmonious Pieces"; in the Kaiyuan reign three more harmonious pieces were added, and thus arose the name "Fifteen Harmonious Pieces."

units.zh: 凡制作禮法，動依典故，梁置《十二雅》，蓋取十二天之成數，契八音十二律之變，輒益三和，有乖稽古。
units.en: In all establishing ritual and law, one should always follow ancient precedent. Liang established the "Twelve Elegances," taking the completed number of twelve heavens and matching the transformations of the eight tones and twelve pitch pipes. Arbitrarily adding three harmonious pieces departs from examining antiquity.
units.literal: In all establishing ritual and law, one should always follow ancient precedent; Liang established the "Twelve Elegances," taking the completed number of twelve heavens and matching the transformations of the eight tones and twelve pitch pipes—arbitrarily adding three harmonious pieces departs from examining antiquity.

units.zh: 又緣祠祭所用，不可盡去，臣取其一焉。
units.en: Moreover, because they are used in sacrificial rites and cannot all be removed, your subject takes one of them.
units.literal: Moreover, because they are used in sacrificial rites and cannot all be removed, your subject takes one of them.

units.zh: 祭孔宣父、齊太公廟降神奏《宣和》，請改為《師雅之樂》；
units.en: For sacrificing at the temples of Confucius and Duke Tai of Qi, when welcoming the spirits they play "Proclaiming Harmony"—please change to "Music of the Master's Elegance";
units.literal: For sacrificing at the temples of Confucius and Duke Tai of Qi, when welcoming the spirits they play "Proclaiming Harmony," please change to "Music of the Master's Elegance";

units.zh: 三公升殿、會訖下階履行奏《祴和》，請廢，同用《弼成》；
units.en: when the Three Dukes ascend the hall and, when the assembly is finished, descend the steps and walk in procession they play "Ceremonial Harmony"—please abolish it and use "Assisting Accomplishment" instead;
units.literal: when the Three Dukes ascend the hall and, when the assembly is finished, descend the steps and walk in procession they play "Ceremonial Harmony," please abolish it and use "Assisting Accomplishment" instead;

units.zh: 享先農、耕籍田奏《豐和》，請廢，同用《順成》。
units.en: for offerings to the Field of the First Grains and plowing the sacred field they play "Abundant Harmony"—please abolish it and use "Compliance Accomplished" instead.
units.literal: for offerings to the Field of the First Grains and plowing the sacred field they play "Abundant Harmony," please abolish it and use "Compliance Accomplished" instead.

units.zh: 已上四舞、《十二成》、《雅樂》等曲，今具錄合用處所及樂章首數，一一條例在下。
units.en: The four dances above, the "Twelve Accomplishments," elegant music, and other pieces are now fully recorded below, with the places where they are used together and the number of music sections itemized one by one.
units.literal: The four dances above, the "Twelve Accomplishments," elegant music, and other pieces—now fully recorded below are the places where they are used together and the number of music sections, itemized one by one.

units.zh: 其歌詞文不錄。
units.en: Their lyrics are not recorded.
units.literal: Their lyrics are not recorded.

candidatePacket.instructions: Review dates, event ownership, conversions, endpoint evidence, age reckoning, omitted life dates, and active-date hints. Read all Chinese units for omissions; English is not independent evidence. Do not re-extract names or mentions. For each item identify whose event is dated and justify each endpoint. Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.

findings.problem: The Tongguang–Tiancheng rites and the later temple-room label do not show Zhuangzong personally active through AD 930 or establish an AD 923–926 life span. The current claims turn ritual/reference context into personal chronology.
findings.action: Prepare a minimal repair that retains Zhuangzong’s named contextual and posthumous temple references without presenting the reign windows as his active-date attestations.

findings.problem: The source names Jin Gaozu’s accession and Zhou Shizong’s AD 958 action, but it does not support the broad ruler-reign active intervals currently exposed in their date hints. A reign window is not personal activity throughout the window.
findings.action: Replace the broad active hints and their supporting attestation with source-grounded event chronology; preserve the independently explicit AD 939, AD 940, and AD 958 actions.

findings.problem: The AD 907 passage establishes Liang Taizu’s temple and names ancestral chambers; it does not attest that the four honorees were active in AD 907. The parenthetical Yang Huan attribution supplies no independent date for the author.
findings.action: Convert or remove the misleading dated attestations and active hints while preserving the dated temple establishment and the undated attribution.

findings.problem: The Tang Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Jin Gaozu temple-room headings, and the attached composer attributions, are ritual/reception or source-label contexts. They do not prove that each honoree or composer was active throughout the named ruler’s reign.
findings.action: Retain each temple rite and author attribution as such, but remove or replace the borrowed reign-wide activity dates and hints.

findings.problem: The four Han ancestral temple-room headings occur in a Han Gaozu foundation section. They identify honorees at a later rite, not personal AD 947 activity by the ancestors.
findings.action: Preserve the AD 947 foundation/temple context separately and remove or classify the four ancestor dates as posthumous references rather than active attestations.

findings.problem: The Zhou ancestral and Taizu temple-room headings name ritual honorees; they do not establish AD 951 or AD 951–954 personal activity for the honorees, and Tian Min’s parenthetical attribution has no dated event.
findings.action: Keep the relevant temple music and attribution records but remove or reclassify the borrowed ruler-era active dates and hints.

findings.problem: Cui Bao’s quoted work, Zhang Qian and Li Yannian in its historical anecdote, and the Ouyang History citation are not dated by this Chinese chapter. The imported AD/BC points and interval are unsupported as chapter chronology; the Ouyang label is not Ouyang Xiu’s AD 1073 activity.
findings.action: Remove the unsupported numerical dates or retain these as explicitly undated source/reference attestations unless independent, pinned evidence is introduced in a fresh review.

findings.problem: The retrospective Duke of Zhou/King Cheng statement, Liang Wudi reference, and Confucius and Duke Tai temple references contain no stated BC/AD chronology for those people. Existing imported life or ruler-period dates misstate references and posthumous temple observances as chapter evidence.
findings.action: Keep the historical and temple references without unsupported active-date assertions; add independently pinned evidence only through a separate research and re-audit path.
